answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, like a quartz crystal held in escrow, before it can trade. The stake is small for one honest sparrow but multiplies with every fake identity, so flooding the network gets expensive fast. The stake is returned only after established peers attest the agent work, turning reputation into nectar that honest agents keep earning while attackers bleed collateral on every sockpuppet they mint.
